title: Non-destructive DNA extraction protocol for minute insects
author: A. Dal Molin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.s7behin
materials: Put 90uL buffer ATL in each microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Reagents
steps.instruction: Verify all necessary materials are available and reagents are prepared.

substeps.instruction: Confirm availability of hot bath or oven, racks, vortex mixer, and centrifuge.
Ensure there is at least 1 set of standard pictures of the specimens.
Check the DNA extraction kit: redissolve precipitates in buffers ATL and AL if necessary.
Ensure ethanol has been added to buffers AW1 and AW2.
Verify sufficient supplies: 1 set of spin columns, 1 extra set of collecting tubes, and 3 sets of microcentrifuge tubes (1 set = number of insect samples).

steps.title: Prepare Samples and Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare the specimens and laboratory hardware for extraction.

substeps.instruction: If insects are stored in alcohol in the freezer, allow samples to reach room temperature.
Label and sterilize (expose to UV) 3 sets of microcentrifuge tubes.
Turn on the hot bath or oven and stabilize at 56°C.

steps.title: Initial Specimen Processing
steps.instruction: Place specimens in lysis buffer and add proteinase K.

substeps.instruction: If applicable, blot alcohol from the specimen using a Kimwipe (allow to dry slightly).
Place the entire insect into a microcentrifuge tube with buffer ATL (use a stereomicroscope if specimens are too small).
Add 10uL proteinase K to each tube for a total volume of 100uL.
Ensure the specimen is in contact with the solution; if stuck to the wall, tap the tube gently on the bench. Do NOT centrifuge.

steps.title: Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples to digest tissues.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 56ºC overnight (at least 8 hours).

steps.title: Extract Recovery
steps.instruction: Separate the DNA extract from the specimen.

substeps.instruction: Label a set of spin columns from the kit and prepare a second set of sterile Eppendorf tubes.
Using a pipette set to approximately 150uL, transfer all fluid (including 'gunk') to a new Eppendorf tube, leaving the insect in the original incubation tube.
Separate the tubes containing the insects and add distilled water; leave insects in water while remaining steps are completed.

steps.title: DNA Purification
steps.instruction: Process the extract through the spin column purification sequence.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the extracts for 15 seconds, add 100uL buffer AL, and vortex again.
Add 100uL 100% ethanol and vortex.
Transfer the mixture (350-400uL) to a DNeasy Mini spin column in a collection tube.
Centrifuge at 8000rpm for 1min.
Add 500uL buffer AW1 to each spin column, centrifuge at 8000rpm for 1min, and discard flow-through (ensure liquid does not touch the bottom of the column).
Add 500uL buffer AW2 to each spin column and centrifuge at 14,000rpm (or maximum possible) for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Column Washing and Elution
steps.instruction: Final wash and elution of the DNA.

substeps.instruction: Discard the collection tube and transfer spin columns to the labeled 1.5uL microcentrifuge tubes.
Discard the collection tube with flow-through and place the spin column in a new 2mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 8,000rpm for 1 minute. Repeat this step (Note: if the insect is too small, do not add more elution buffer to avoid dilution).
Add 100uL buffer AE to each spin column and incubate at room temperature for 1-2 minutes.
Store extracts in a -20°C freezer.

steps.title: Voucher Specimen Recovery
steps.instruction: Clean and dehydrate the specimen for mounting.

substeps.instruction: Observe the specimen under a stereomicroscope and use a pipette to remove it from the water.
Place the specimen in small plates or tubes with water for the dehydration series and check for integrity.
Perform ethanol dehydration starting with pure water, gradually increasing ethanol concentrations (30%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 100%) until reaching absolute alcohol.
Proceed to card-mount or slide-mount (weakly sclerotized specimens should be moved to slides).
